reading: Two solid rectangles face each other across a gap; the gap between them is filled with 8, narrowed by one cell at each end of their overlap.

new_rows.name: between_inner
new_rows.datalog:
isfg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !isfg(Y, X).
hl(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y, X2, C), X2 < X.
hr(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y, X2, C), X2 > X.
hb(Y, X) :- hl(Y, X), hr(Y, X).
vu(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y2, X, C), Y2 < Y.
vd(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), cell(Y2, X, C), Y2 > Y.
vb(Y, X) :- vu(Y, X), vd(Y, X).
between_inner(Y, X) :- hb(Y, X), Ya = Y - 1, Yb = Y + 1, hb(Ya, X), hb(Yb, X).
between_inner(Y, X) :- vb(Y, X), Xa = X - 1, Xb = X + 1, vb(Y, Xa), vb(Y, Xb).

why: every between cell that has between cells on both sides across the gap direction becomes 8; nothing else changes

reading: Diamond rings are resized about their centres: colour-2 rings shrink by one step (a radius-1 ring becomes a single cell), colour-5 rings grow by one step (a single cell becomes a ring); rings of other colours stay.

slots.subject: each diamond-ring object (8-connected, one colour)
slots.centre: the ring's centre, may lie off-grid

why: each 2 ring has radius one less and each 5 ring radius one more, same centre; other objects identical
invariants: rings of colours other than 2 and 5

reading: Each closed loop of 1 gets a ring of 2 drawn around its outside and a ring of 3 lining its inside; loops with a gap (not closed) are left alone.

slots.subject: 1-coloured objects that enclose background
slots.outer: background cells touching the loop from outside (8-neighbour) -> 2
slots.inner: enclosed background cells touching the loop -> 3

why: only closed loops change; their outer neighbour ring is 2 and inner neighbour ring is 3
invariants: enclosed cells not touching the loop

reading: The grid is a 4x6 array of 3x3 glyphs; every 1-glyph with the same shape as the one 8 glyph turns 8, then every glyph lying strictly between two 8 glyphs in the same glyph row or column turns 7 (keeping its shape).

slots.cells: 3x3 glyph slots separated by background rows/cols
slots.between: glyphs strictly between two 8 glyphs on a glyph row/column -> 7

why: glyph shapes never change; only their colour changes to 8 (same shape as exemplar) or 7 (between two 8s)

reading: Two small blocks sit at opposite ends of a uniform grid; each grows toward the other, filling its half of the gap, one cell wider on each side than the block, leaving a single background line in the middle when the gap is odd.

slots.fill: gap between them split in half, each half in the nearer block's colour
slots.width: block span plus one cell on each side (only over the gap)
slots.middle: one background line left when the gap length is odd

why: the gap is split evenly between the two colours; blocks themselves unchanged
invariants: cells outside the gap's widened band

reading: A shape is split by one empty row or column running through it; that whole grid line is painted 3.

new_rows.name: gap_line
new_rows.datalog:
miny(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
maxy(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
minx(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
rowfg(Y) :- cell(Y, X, C).
colfg(X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
gaprow(Y) :- px(Y, X, C), miny(A), maxy(B), Y > A, Y < B, !rowfg(Y).
gapcol(X) :- px(Y, X, C), minx(A), maxx(B), X > A, X < B, !colfg(X).
gap_line(Y, X) :- gaprow(Y), px(Y, X, C).
gap_line(Y, X) :- gapcol(X), px(Y, X, C).

why: the empty row/column strictly inside the shape's bounding box is entirely 3; nothing else changes

reading: On a dotted lattice, a dotted rectangle becomes a solid outline with a plain interior; the small dotted pieces outside it become solid blocks (their bounding boxes) packed inside it in input order along its longer side, one-cell gaps, centred; the pieces are erased from outside.

slots.container: the rectangle drawn in lattice dots of one colour
slots.packing: solid bounding boxes, in order of position, along the interior's longer axis, 1-cell gaps, centred
slots.cleanup: interior lattice -> line background colour; old piece sites restored to lattice

why: output = lattice + solid outline + centred row/column of solid piece boxes inside

reading: A 1 dropped from the top row falls into the 2 container; if it lands in a sealed cup the cup's interior fills with 1, otherwise (misses or the cup's floor leaks) the whole bottom row becomes 1. The dropped 1 is removed.

slots.source: the single 1 in the top row (its column)
slots.held: cup interior between walls, above floor, up to wall top -> 1

why: exactly one of: the cup under the drop column is sealed and filled, or the bottom row is all 1

reading: Each 9 square of side s gets a 3 frame of thickness s/2 around it and a 1 shadow, as wide as the square, running from it down to the bottom edge; frames are drawn over shadows and squares over both.

slots.subject: each 9 square
slots.shadow: colour 1, square's columns, from below the square to the bottom border

why: squares keep place; every frame and shadow follows the square's size

reading: Any two 1 cells on the same row or column are joined by a line of 8 through the background between them.
why: every background cell between two 1s on a row or column is 8; nothing else changes
